business_summary: NVIDIA designs and sells the computing systems that AI runs on. It does not own factories (fabless): it designs GPUs and networking chips, TSMC manufactures them, and NVIDIA sells them as chips, boards, and whole rack-scale systems (e.g. GB300/Blackwell Ultra) together with its software stack. Buyers are cloud providers (hyperscalers), AI labs, neoclouds, enterprises, governments, and PC/workstation makers. As of Q1 FY2027 NVIDIA reports two market platforms: Data Center (with Hyperscale and ACIE sub-markets) and Edge Computing. Data Center is essentially the whole company - $75.2B of $81.6B revenue in Q1 FY2027 (92% of total, +92% y/y); Edge Computing was $6.4B (+29% y/y). Full fiscal 2026 (ended 2026-01-25) revenue was $215.938B, up 65%, with Data Center $193.7B. Q1 FY2027 revenue was $81.615B, up 85% y/y, and management guided Q2 FY2027 to $91.0B +/- 2%. The reason to expect NVIDIA still to be winning in 5-10 years is CUDA: nearly two decades of accumulated software libraries, frameworks, compilers and trained developers that make NVIDIA hardware the default target for AI work, reinforced now by a full-stack advantage (GPU + NVLink + InfiniBand/Spectrum-X networking + systems software) that rivals must replicate in its entirety, not piece by piece. The honest counterweight is that NVIDIA's largest customers are also its most motivated would-be competitors.

moat.type: CUDA software ecosystem and developer lock-in (highest switching cost in the stack); full-stack rack-scale systems advantage (GPU + NVLink + networking + software) that competitors must match end-to-end; scale and priority access to constrained TSMC CoWoS and HBM supply; an annual product cadence rivals struggle to match. Caveat on durability: unlike a consumer brand, this moat depends on staying at the technology frontier every ~12 months, and the largest customers are funding in-house substitutes (Google TPU, Amazon Trainium, Meta MTIA) and open software layers (Triton, ROCm, MLIR) explicitly designed to erode CUDA lock-in.

quality.gross_margin: 71.1% GAAP for FY2026 (gross profit $153.463B / revenue $215.938B); 74.9% GAAP in Q1 FY2027; FY2026 was depressed by the $4.5B H20 excess-inventory charge taken in Q1 FY2026 (Q1 FY2026 GAAP gross margin was 60.5%). Q2 FY2027 guided to 74.9% GAAP +/- 50bp.

Exceptionally high because the model is fabless and capital-light (FY2026 capex only $6.042B, 2.8% of revenue). Treat the exact figure as an estimate, not a filed number.
quality.net_debt_to_ebitda: Net cash, approximately -0.3x. At 2026-04-26 total debt was $8.470B ($1.000B short-term + $7.470B long-term) versus cash $13.237B + marketable debt securities $37.098B = $50.335B, i.e. ~$41.9B net cash. FY2026 EBITDA ~= operating income $130.387B + D&A $2.843B = ~$133.2B.
quality.fcf_positive: Yes, strongly. FY2026 FCF ~$96.7B (operating cash flow $102.718B - capex $6.042B). Trailing twelve months to 2026-04-26 FCF ~$119.1B (FY2026 $96.676B - Q1 FY2026 $26.187B + Q1 FY2027 $48.587B), ~$4.88 per diluted share on 24.391B Q1 FY2027 diluted shares.

valuation.method: Blend of two trailing-twelve-month methods, computed by code/valuation.py. (1) P/E: TTM GAAP diluted EPS $6.53 (= FY2026 $4.90 - Q1 FY2026 $0.76 + Q1 FY2027 $2.39, all from filings) x multiples 25 / 33 / 42 -> $163.25 / $215.49 / $274.26. Multiples chosen because a business compounding revenue 65-85% with >70% gross margin, >100% ROIC and net cash has historically commanded 30-45x, while its semiconductor cyclicality and 54% top-three-customer concentration justify a 25x downside case. (2) FCF yield: TTM FCF/share $4.88 at target yields 3.5% / 2.7% / 2.1% -> $139.43 / $180.74 / $232.38. Blended band low $151.34 / base $198.12 / high $253.32; margin of safety at $223.93 is -13.0% (i.e. the stock trades ~13% ABOVE our base fair value). IMPORTANT CAVEAT, both directions: (a) trailing EPS of $6.53 is FLATTERED by non-operating gains - Q1 FY2027 alone contained $16.0B of unrealized gains on equity investments (~$0.55/share after tax) and FY2026 contained $11.063B of non-operating income; core operating TTM EPS is closer to $5.61. (b) Trailing numbers also badly LAG a business growing 85% y/y: annualising the company's own Q2 FY2027 guidance (revenue $91.0B x 74.9% GAAP gross margin - $8.5B GAAP opex = ~$59.7B quarterly operating income, +~$0.44B net interest, taxed at 17%, over ~24.3B diluted shares) gives ~$2.05 quarterly, ~$8.2 annualised forward EPS - at which $223.93 is ~27x forward earnings, and sell-side consensus FY2027 EPS is $9.00 (aggregator). We deliberately anchor the published band on trailing, filed numbers and treat the forward case as upside evidence rather than as our base case.

bull_case: CUDA is the deepest software moat in computing infrastructure: two decades of libraries, frameworks and trained developers mean the switching cost is measured in engineer-years, not dollars.
NVIDIA has moved from selling chips to selling whole AI factories - GPU, NVLink, InfiniBand/Spectrum-X networking and systems software - so a competitor must beat the entire rack, not one component.

Economics are close to best-in-class anywhere: FY2026 gross margin 71.1% (74.9% in Q1 FY2027), operating margin 60.4% (op income $130.387B on $215.938B revenue), ROIC well above 100%, capex only 2.8% of revenue.

Fortress balance sheet: ~$41.9B net cash at 2026-04-26 with only $8.47B of debt; the company is buying back stock aggressively ($19.3B repurchased in Q1 FY2027 alone) and the board added $80.0B to the buyback authorisation on 2026-05-18.

Demand visibility is still accelerating, not decelerating: Q1 FY2027 revenue +85% y/y and Q2 FY2027 guided to $91.0B, and management stated that guidance assumes ZERO Data Center compute revenue from China - so China is optionality, not an embedded assumption.
Free cash flow is real and enormous - ~$119B trailing twelve months, ~87% of core NOPAT - which is much harder to manufacture than accounting earnings.
risks: Extreme customer concentration: in Q1 FY2027 three direct customers were 21%, 17% and 16% of total revenue (54% combined), up from two customers at 16% and 14% a year earlier. Losing or being designed out by any one of them is a double-digit revenue event.

Those same customers are NVIDIA's competitors. Google (TPU), Amazon (Trainium), Meta (MTIA) and others are spending heavily on in-house accelerators explicitly to reduce NVIDIA dependence; AMD and open software layers attack CUDA from the other side.

This is a capital-expenditure cycle, not an annuity. NVIDIA's revenue is a function of a handful of companies' AI capex budgets. Semiconductor demand has historically overshot and then corrected hard, and a slowdown in AI capex would hit revenue, gross margin and inventory simultaneously.

Quality of earnings is degrading. Q1 FY2027 GAAP net income of $58.321B EXCEEDED operating income of $53.536B because of $16.0B of unrealized gains on equity stakes ($13.4B public + $2.6B non-marketable). These are mark-to-market paper gains that can reverse; headline GAAP EPS of $2.39 versus non-GAAP $1.87 overstates the operating business.

Circular / vendor-financing exposure. Non-marketable securities went from $22.251B (2026-01-25) to $43.364B (2026-04-26) after $18.582B of purchases in a single quarter, and marketable equity securities went from $12.886B to $30.237B. NVIDIA is increasingly investing in the same AI companies that buy its chips; if those companies cannot fund themselves independently, both the investment value and the revenue disappear together.

China is effectively closed. The FY2026 10-K states NVIDIA was 'effectively foreclosed from competing in China's data center computing/compute market'. H200 licences granted from February 2026 had produced no revenue as of the Q1 FY2027 filing, carry a 25% US import tariff on inspected units, and US officials have expressed an expectation of taking 15%+ of licensed China revenue. In August 2026 US authorities began reviewing Chinese firms' offshore access to NVIDIA chips.

Inventory and non-cancellable purchase obligations are ballooning: inventories rose from $21.403B to $25.797B in one quarter, with $3.121B of accrued excess-inventory purchase obligations. The Q1 FY2026 $4.5B H20 write-off is the template for what a demand or policy shock does to this balance sheet.

Valuation offers no cushion. At $223.93 the stock is ~34x trailing GAAP EPS and ~46x trailing FCF, ~13% above our base fair value and ~15% above its 200-day average of $193.97. We would be paying full price for peak-cycle economics.
Single-supplier dependence on TSMC (and on a concentrated HBM supply base) creates geopolitical and capacity risk NVIDIA does not control.
what_would_break_thesis: Data Center revenue declines year-over-year in two consecutive quarters (the core engine is rolling over).
Total company revenue declines year-over-year in two consecutive quarters.
GAAP gross margin falls below 65% for two consecutive quarters (pricing power or cost structure has broken).

Inventory write-downs plus excess-inventory purchase-obligation charges exceed $5B in any single quarter, or inventories grow faster than revenue for three consecutive quarters (a repeat of the Q1 FY2026 H20 pattern).
Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow falls below 50% of trailing-twelve-month operating income for two consecutive quarters (earnings stop converting to cash).
The net cash position of ~$41.9B turns into net debt, or net-debt-to-EBITDA rises above 1.0x.

Non-marketable plus marketable equity 'strategic' investments exceed 30% of total assets (they were 28.3% at 2026-04-26: $43.364B + $30.237B = $73.601B of $259.474B), OR the company discloses that vendor-financed customers are a material driver of revenue growth - the circular-financing red flag.
Top-three direct-customer concentration rises above 70% of revenue while total revenue growth decelerates below 20% year-over-year, or NVIDIA discloses the loss of a >10% customer.
A major customer publicly commits the majority of a new training or inference cluster generation to non-NVIDIA silicon.
Any accounting restatement, material weakness in internal controls, disputed auditor change, or a pattern of GAAP net income persistently exceeding operating income because of investment marks.
TRIM (not a full sell) trigger: price exceeds the top of the fair-value band ($253.32) without a corresponding, filing-evidenced increase in earnings power.
catalysts: Q2 FY2027 results on 2026-08-26 - the single most important near-term data point; guidance is $91.0B revenue, and the shape of H2 FY2027 guidance will tell us whether the cycle is still accelerating.
Rubin-generation product ramp and any evidence that the annual cadence is holding against AMD and in-house ASICs.
Any real, revenue-producing reopening of the China data-center market under the H200 licence regime (currently zero revenue and excluded from guidance - pure optionality).
Continued execution of the $80.0B incremental buyback authorised 2026-05-18, which shrinks the share count at ~$220 levels.
A market-wide AI de-rating or a capex-guidance cut from a hyperscaler pulling the price toward the low end of our band ($151-$180), which is where this becomes a genuinely attractive purchase.
